# Warlock AI Workspace

> Package: `@warlock.js/ai-workspace`

> Policy-jailed filesystem + shell workspace for @warlock.js/ai agents

## Skills

- [Package orientation](@warlock.js/ai-workspace/skills/index.md): Policy-jailed filesystem and shell access for @warlock.js/ai agents, for coding and build-loop agents. Exports `workspace`, `makeEditFileTool`, `makeRunShellTool`, `makeRunTestsTool`, `createLocalBackend`, `createMockBackend`, `WorkspacePolicyError`. Use for: let an agent read, edit or write files, run shell commands or tests safely, sandbox an agent to a directory, build a coding agent that loops until tests pass, test file tools with a fake backend. Not this package: web, HTTP or MCP tools → @warlock.js/ai-tools; agents and custom tools → @warlock.js/ai; tracing runs → @warlock.js/ai-panoptic.
- [build-loop-agent](@warlock.js/ai-workspace/build-loop-agent/SKILL.md): Wire a @warlock.js/ai-workspace into a coding agent that closes the read → edit → run-tests loop on its own. Triggers: `ws.tools.all()`, `ai.agent({ tools: ws.tools.all() })`, `maxTrips`, `run_tests`, `run_shell`, 'agent that fixes a failing test', 'make the suite green', 'coding agent that edits a repo', 'build-loop agent', 'self-correcting agent', 'read-only code reviewer', 'scaffold then hand off to an agent', 'share one workspace across a supervisor', 'least-privilege agent tools', 'errors as tool data'; typical wiring `const ws = ai.workspace({ cwd, shell }); ai.agent({ model, tools: ws.tools.all(), maxTrips })`. Skip: constructing the workspace / its policy / direct methods / readonly / scope — the `use-a-workspace` topic; the agent loop / maxTrips / events themselves — the `run-ai-agent` topic of the `warlock-js-ai` skill.
- [use-a-workspace](@warlock.js/ai-workspace/use-a-workspace/SKILL.md): Build and operate a policy-jailed filesystem + shell workspace with @warlock.js/ai-workspace. Triggers: `ai.workspace`, `workspace(`, `WorkspacePolicy`, `WorkspaceShellPolicy`, `WorkspaceToolName`, `ws.tools.all`, `ws.tools.pick`, `ws.readFile`, `ws.writeFile`, `ws.editFile`, `ws.exec`, `ws.grep`, `ws.glob`, `ws.readonly`, `ws.scope`, `ws.multiEdit`, `ws.listDir`, `ws.startShell`, `ws.shellOutput`, `ws.shellKill`, `ws.dispose`, `ws.readTodos`, `ws.writeTodos`, `WorkspacePolicyError`, `WorkspaceEditError`, `WorkspaceJobError`, `WorkspaceShellRefusalReason`, `checkShellCommand`, `denyPaths`, `denyPatterns`, `allowCommand`, `interpreter`, `shell.background`, `list.ignore`, `inheritEnv`, `expectHash`, `read.maxBytes`, `bytesCapped`, `cancelled`, `ExecOptions`, `tokenizeCommand`, `read_file`/`edit_file`/`multi_edit`/`write_file`/`list_dir`/`run_shell`/`shell_output`/`shell_kill`/`run_tests`/`grep`/`todo_write`/`todo_read`; 'give an agent file tools', 'jail an agent to a directory', 'let an agent read/write/grep a repo', 'read-only workspace for a reviewer', 'scope an agent to a subdirectory', 'run a shell command under policy', 'edit a file with a stale-hash guard', 'command injection guard for an agent shell tool', 'ReDoS-safe grep for an agent', 'cap how many bytes a read returns', 'cancel a running workspace command', 'let the agent use pipes and &&', 'why was my shell command refused', 'deny git push --force', 'run a dev server in the background', 'atomic multi-edit', 'list a directory for an agent', 'todo list tool for an agent'; typical import `import "@warlock.js/ai-workspace"; import { ai } from "@warlock.js/ai"`. Skip: building the agent loop that consumes the tools — the `build-loop-agent` topic; defining a non-filesystem custom tool — the `define-ai-tool` topic of the `warlock-js-ai` skill.
